subject: English Language

questions.prompt: What did the Princess like doing? (A walk, B pick, C pick flowers and watch birds, D walk alone, E fight)
steps: The included listening script on page 4 directly states these evening activities.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: C. Picking flowers and watching birds.

questions.prompt: Who captured the Princess? (A brave man, B bad men, C poor boy, D group of men, E king)
steps: The last sentence of the script uses this description.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: When did the story take place? (A once, B long time, C once upon a time, D during Covid-19, E unknown)
steps: The script opens with this traditional story phrase, giving no exact date.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Where was the palace garden? (A near post office, B close to forest, C in forest, D inside palace, E above water)
steps: The script explicitly locates the garden near the forest.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: How long did she stay in the forest? (A until morning, B until, C until dark, D all night, E did not go)
steps: The script says she stayed until it became dark.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Which structure makes a past simple sentence? (A N/p+mv, B have+mv, C S+mv-s, D S+will/shall+V+O, E mv in past+O)
steps: A complete affirmative sentence needs a subject and a finite past verb; the printed alternatives do not state the full rule clearly.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Required complete structure: subject + past-tense main verb + object/complement. E indicates the intended past verb but omits the subject.

questions.prompt: Does giraffe ___ only vegetation? (A ate, B eats, C eaten, D feeds, E fed)
steps: Does must be followed by the base verb eat or feed on; all printed verb forms are unsuitable.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: No correct option. Corrected: Does a giraffe eat only vegetation?

questions.prompt: The children ___ played since yesterday. (A played, B plays, C has, D play, E have)
steps: A plural subject takes have before the past participle played.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: My nephew comes home late. Which pronoun replaces my nephew? (A he, B she, C herself, D itself, E they)
steps: Nephew is the male family term, so he is intended.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: I prefer eating bananas ___ rice. (A and, B at, C with, D for, E to)
steps: Prefer X to Y compares preferences; with would instead mean eating the foods together.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Mr. Mtango comes to school ___ motorcycle. (A with, B into, C on, D by, E at)
steps: Use by before a means of transport without an article.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Simba played ___ African sports. (A against, B with, C by, D at, E along)
steps: Against identifies the opposing team.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: A. Against is intended; with is grammatical in a shared-play sense.

questions.prompt: ___ Mainda ___ Kamtoni finished the assignment. (A neither/nor, B either/or, C neither/or, D either/or, E neither/either)
steps: Both pairs are correct conjunctions; no context states whether neither or one of them finished.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: A. Neither...nor, or B/D. either...or, depending on intended meaning.

questions.prompt: They will ___ to Mtwara. (A went, B gone, C going, D go, E run)
steps: Will takes a base verb; go expresses travel generally.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: D. Go (intended); E. run is also grammatical.

questions.prompt: He was making noise ___ the teacher was teaching. (A and, B as, C when, D while, E during)
steps: While clearly expresses simultaneous ongoing actions.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: D. While is intended; as and when can also join these actions.

questions.prompt: I have been here ___ a long period. (A since, B behind, C to, D of, E for)
steps: For introduces duration; since introduces a starting point.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: I saw a dog ___ I was on my way home. (A while, B on, C when, D in, E to)
steps: Both conjunctions can connect the sighting with the journey.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: ___ you work hard, you will receive gifts. (A if, B unless, C although, D in spite of, E though)
steps: If introduces the positive condition for the reward.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: She ___ to swim every Friday. (A love, B loves, C loved, D is loving)
steps: The third-person present form is loves; past loved would need a past context.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: B. Loves, for a current habit.

questions.prompt: An elephant is ___ than a lion. (A big, B biggest, C large, D bigger, E too big)
steps: Than takes the comparative bigger.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: I saw her pen ___ the chair. (A on, B at, C by, D above [printed obove], E under)
steps: No picture or location clue is supplied, so a preposition cannot be prescribed uniquely.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: No unique answer: on, by, above or under can describe different positions.

questions.prompt: Cornell ___ to jail. (A has been taken, B have been taken, C is, D in, E will)
steps: Cornell is singular; has been taken is a complete passive verb phrase.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: They ___ fly Singapore next Friday night. (A go, B shall, C use, D should, E can)
steps: Next Friday supports future intention, but it does not rule out advice or ability.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: B. Shall is the intended future auxiliary; should/can are also grammatical with other meanings. Corrected: fly to Singapore.

questions.prompt: ___ she works fast, she will not finish. (A if, B unless, C since, D for, E should)
steps: Unless means if she does not; the source also needs works instead of work.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Hour hand is just before 8; minute hand is at 10. What time is it? (A seven minutes to ten, B 7:10, C 8:50, D ten minutes to seven, E ten minutes to eight)
steps: At 10 the minute hand shows 50 minutes; the approaching hour is 8.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Ally would come ___ he had permission. (A unless, B if, C but, D because, E although)
steps: Would plus if and past tense expresses a hypothetical condition.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: B. If, for the intended condition.

questions.prompt: I came here ___ to see Juma. (A because, B in ordered to, C in order, D in order that, E in order to)
steps: To is already printed after the blank, so in order makes in order to without doubling to.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: If we ___ a yacht, we would sail the Indian Ocean. (A have, B had, C has, D haven't, E hasn't)
steps: A hypothetical conditional uses if + past and would + base verb.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Give the opposite of above. (A below, B blown, C under, D front, E up)
steps: Above and below are the standard opposite pair; under has a related lower-position meaning.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: What means help? (A assist, B hard, C aids, D service, E add)
steps: Assist is the matching base-form synonym.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: That pond is the ___ in the area. (A shallow, B shallower, C shallowest, D shallowed, E shallowing)
steps: Use the superlative for comparison with all ponds in the area.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: The kindergarten pupils will ___ soon. (A graduation, B graduate, C graduated, D party, E ceremony)
steps: Will takes a base verb; graduate means complete a course.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: What does your mother's daughter call your mother? (A stepmother, B guardian, C mother, D aunt, E grandmother)
steps: The woman is the daughter's mother too.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: The bottle is ___ the table. I left it there this morning. (A over, B in, C under, D besides, E on)
steps: On describes resting on the tabletop; no printed clue establishes its location.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: E. On is likely intended; over/under are also possible without a picture.

questions.prompt: A crowd is a group of ___. (A stars, B clouds, C people, D army, E pupils)
steps: Crowd generally names many people gathered together.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: C. People (general answer); a crowd of pupils is also possible.

questions.prompt: Order with A-E: Moses advised his sister to use the library to improve her grades.
steps: Finish with the advice after discussing the library.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: The library has many books arranged on shelves.
steps: This detail follows the library definition.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: Aziza said a library is a big room where books are kept for readers.
steps: Give the definition after introducing their conversation.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: One day Aziza and Moses talked about the school library.
steps: The conversation follows introduction of the pupils.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: Moses and Aziza are Standard Five pupils.
steps: Introduce the characters first.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Which bird is the largest in the world?
steps: The comprehension passage explicitly identifies it.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: What foods do birds eat, according to the passage?
steps: Copy the diet list; it describes different birds, not every bird eating every food.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Nectar, fruits, plant seeds and small animals, including other birds.

questions.prompt: What are birds kept at home called?
steps: The final paragraph gives this term.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Which two products do hens and ducks give us?
steps: The final sentence names both products.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: What weight can a fully grown ostrich reach in the passage?
steps: The passage states this upper weight, rather than claiming every ostrich weighs 156 kg.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

summaries.Listening and grammar: Listen to the supplied teacher text and identify the exact detail asked for. Check spelling and sentence punctuation; missing scripts are explicitly identified.
summaries.Grammar and vocabulary: Use sentence meaning, subject agreement and time clues to choose the word or verb form. Apply the specific rule explained for each task and note ambiguous choices.
summaries.Composition and comprehension: Find evidence in the passage or poem before answering. Distinguish explicit statements, reasonable inferences and model interpretations.

references.title: Standard Five Exams | 2010 - 2023 | Monthly, Midterm, Terminal and Annual Exams - Download All Subjects - Msomi Bora

limitations: 6: Printed structure options omit or obscure essential past-simple sentence elements.
7: No base-form verb is supplied after does.
13: Neither/nor and duplicate either/or choices are all structurally possible.
21,34: No diagram or location clue makes the preposition unique.
23: Destination lacks to and several modal meanings are possible.
